name: Hand building
summary: A vessel or a figure is built from coils, slabs or pinched lumps of clay, with no wheel. The maker joins the parts with slip and keeps the marks of the hand.
how: Roll coils or cut slabs of clay.
Score the edges and press the parts together with slip.
Smooth the joins, or leave them as part of the form.
Dry the piece slowly, then fire it.

origin.note: The oldest fired pots, which are more than 10000 years old, are hand-built because the wheel is not yet known.

adoptions.via: Californian sculptors build large glazed figures and objects by hand, and keep thumb marks and cracks as part of the joke.
